taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station BMGS-bori-field, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1005 | 3.42 | 3.42
2 | 3588 | 6.33 | 9.76
3 | 1358 | 10.9 | 20.7
4 | 333 | 9.08 | 29.7
5 | 2950 | 36.8 | 66.5
6 | 5469 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as H-type.

Is this label correct for these layer values? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"label_correct": true or false, "curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the correct curve-type notation, we evaluate each consecutive set of three layers:

1. **Layers 1-2-3:** $\rho_1 (1005) < \rho_2 (3588) > \rho_3 (1358) \rightarrow \mathbf{K}$
2. **Layers 2-3-4:** $\rho_2 (3588) > \rho_3 (1358) > \rho_4 (333) \rightarrow \mathbf{Q}$
3. **Layers 3-4-5:** $\rho_3 (1358) > \rho_4 (333) < \rho_5 (2950) \rightarrow \mathbf{H}$
4. **Layers 4-5-6:** $\rho_4 (333) < \rho_5 (2950) < \rho_6 (5469) \rightarrow \mathbf{A}$

The full curve classification is **KQHA**, so the file label of H-type is incorrect.

{"label_correct": false, "curve_type": "KQHA"}
